questions.question: Define KVL and KCL.

paragraphs: Kirchhoff’s laws are used with Ohm’s law to analyse electrical networks.
bullets: Kirchhoff’s Current Law (KCL): the algebraic sum of currents at a node is zero; equivalently, total current entering a node equals total current leaving it.
Kirchhoff’s Voltage Law (KVL): the algebraic sum of all voltage rises and drops around any closed loop is zero.
answer.note: A simple KCL example is \(I_1+I_2=I_3+I_4\). A simple KVL example is \(V_s=IR_1+IR_2\) for two series resistors.

questions.question: Draw the impedance triangle of series RLC Circuit.

paragraphs: For a series RLC circuit the complex impedance is \(Z=R+j(X_L-X_C)\). The impedance triangle has resistance on the horizontal axis, net reactance on the vertical axis and \(|Z|\) as the hypotenuse.
answer.note: If \(X_L>X_C\), the triangle is inductive and the vertical side is upward; if \(X_C>X_L\), the net reactance is capacitive.

questions.r25_mapping: Unit III · DC motor speed control
questions.question: List the speed control techniques of DC Motor.

bullets: Field/flux control: vary field current; weakening flux raises speed and is used for speeds above rated speed.
Armature-voltage control: vary the armature supply voltage with flux held approximately constant; used for speeds below rated speed.
Armature-resistance control: add series resistance in the armature circuit to reduce speed; simple but inefficient.

questions.question: Briefly explain the electrical characteristics of lead acid battery.

bullets: A single lead-acid cell gives about 2.1 V nominally; the fully charged open-circuit value is stated as about 2.2 V.
Terminal voltage falls during discharge and should not be allowed to fall below about 1.8 V per cell.
Capacity is specified in ampere-hours (Ah) and decreases as discharge rate increases.
Ampere-hour efficiency is typically about 90–95%; watt-hour efficiency is lower than Ah efficiency.
equations: \[\eta_{Ah}=\frac{\text{Ah delivered on discharge}}{\text{Ah absorbed on charge}}\times100\]

questions.question: State PN junction diode and draw its V-I Characteristics.

paragraphs: A PN junction diode is formed by joining p-type and n-type semiconductor regions. The junction forms a depletion region and a built-in potential barrier.

In forward bias, the applied voltage reduces the barrier. Current is initially small and then rises rapidly after the knee/cut-in region. In reverse bias, the barrier widens and only a small reverse saturation current flows until breakdown is reached.

steps: The 40 Ω and 20 Ω resistors are in series: \(40+20=60\,\Omega\).

questions.question: Find the current through the 4 Ω resistor by applying Superposition theorem.

figures.description: Circuit diagram supplied with Question 2: the network used to find the current through the 4 Ω resistor by superposition.
figures.alt: 2023–24 Unit I Q2 circuit with a 5 A current source, 20 V voltage source, 2 ohm and 5 ohm resistors, two 6 ohm resistors and a 4 ohm load branch.

paragraphs: Take downward current through the 4 Ω resistor as positive. Use superposition by activating one independent source at a time.
steps: 5 A source acting alone: replace the 20 V source by a short circuit. Let the top node be \(V_T\) and the middle node between the two 6 Ω resistors be \(V_M\). The 5 A source forces 5 A through the 2 Ω branch into the top node.
Node equations are \((V_T-V_M)/6+V_T/4=5\) and \((V_M-V_T)/6+V_M/6+V_M/5=0\). Solving gives \(V_T=96/7\,V\), hence \(I_{4,5A}=V_T/4=24/7\,A\) downward.
20 V source acting alone: open the 5 A current source. The 2 Ω branch then carries no current. The node equations are \((V_T-V_M)/6+V_T/4=0\) and \((V_M-V_T)/6+V_M/6+(V_M-20)/5=0\).

questions.question: A Voltage of 120 V at 50 Hz is applied to a resistance R in series with a capacitance C. The current drawn is 2 A and power loss in the resistance is 100 W. Calculate the (i) Resistance (ii) Capacitance and (iii) Power factor of the circuit.

steps: For a series RC circuit, \(|Z|^2=R^2+X_C^2\), so \(X_C=\sqrt{60^2-25^2}=54.544\,\Omega\).
Power factor \(=R/|Z|=25/60=0.4167\). Since the circuit is capacitive, current leads voltage.

questions.question: Explain the Principle of Operation and Working of single-phase transformer with neat diagrams.

paragraphs: A transformer is a static device that transfers AC electrical energy from one circuit to another at the same frequency by electromagnetic induction.

When AC is applied to the primary winding, a small magnetising current produces alternating core flux. This flux links both windings and induces emfs in the primary and secondary according to Faraday’s law. If a load is connected to the secondary, secondary current flows and the primary draws the additional current needed to balance the secondary ampere-turns.
bullets: If \(N_2>N_1\), it is step-up; if \(N_2<N_1\), it is step-down.
A transformer does not operate on steady DC because steady DC does not create alternating flux.
answer.diagram: AC supply V1 → [Primary N1] ║ laminated iron core ║ [Secondary N2] → Load

question_parts.label: a
question_parts.content: Derive the Expression for Generator EMF Equation.

question_parts.label: b
question_parts.content: Explain the Working of DC Motor with neat diagrams.

parts.label: a
paragraphs: Let \(P\) be the number of poles, \(\Phi\) flux per pole, \(Z\) total armature conductors, \(N\) speed in rpm and \(A\) parallel paths.
bullets: For lap winding, \(A=P\).
For wave winding, \(A=2\).
steps: Flux cut by one conductor in one revolution = \(P\Phi\) Wb.
Average emf induced in one conductor = \(P\Phi /(60/N)=P\Phi N/60\) V.
Conductors in series per parallel path = \(Z/A\).

parts.label: b
paragraphs: A DC motor converts electrical energy into mechanical energy. A current-carrying armature conductor placed in the magnetic field of the poles experiences a force. The forces on conductors on opposite sides of the armature form a torque and rotate the armature.

The direction of force is given by Fleming’s left-hand rule. The commutator reverses current in the appropriate armature conductors every half-turn so that developed torque remains in the same rotational direction.
As the armature rotates, it also cuts magnetic flux and generates an emf opposing the supply. This is the back emf.
bullets: Back emf automatically limits armature current as speed rises.
At starting \(E_b=0\), so starting current would be large unless limited.

question_parts.label: a
question_parts.content: Explain the principle of operation of Three phase Induction Motor.

question_parts.label: b
question_parts.content: List the differences between Squirrel cage Induction Motor and slip ring induction motor.

parts.label: a
paragraphs: A balanced three-phase supply to the stator windings produces a rotating magnetic field (RMF). The RMF rotates at synchronous speed.

Because the rotor initially has relative motion with respect to the RMF, an emf is induced in the short-circuited rotor conductors. Rotor current flows, and interaction of rotor current with the stator field produces torque in the direction of the RMF.
The rotor cannot reach synchronous speed in motoring operation: at synchronous speed the relative speed would be zero, rotor emf and rotor current would vanish, and therefore torque would be zero.
parts.result: The induction motor therefore runs slightly below synchronous speed with non-zero slip.

rows: Three-phase insulated rotor winding connected to slip rings
Can be added through slip rings
Higher when external resistance is used
Can be controlled using rotor resistance
Higher because of brushes and slip rings

question_parts.label: a
question_parts.content: With neat Diagrams explain the working of MCB.

question_parts.label: b
question_parts.content: Define Earthing and Explain Its Types.

parts.label: a
paragraphs: An MCB (Miniature Circuit Breaker) is a resettable protective device that automatically opens a circuit during overload or short circuit.
bullets: Overload protection: current heats a bimetal strip; it bends and releases the trip mechanism after a time delay.
Short-circuit protection: a high fault current energises the magnetic trip strongly and opens the contacts almost instantaneously.
The arc formed when contacts separate is driven into an arc chute and extinguished. After the fault is cleared, the MCB can be reset.
parts.diagram:
Line → [thermal bimetal] → [magnetic trip] → moving contact → Load
                         ↘ trip latch / arc chute

parts.label: b
paragraphs: Earthing connects exposed metallic parts of electrical equipment to the earth through a low-resistance conductor and electrode.
bullets: It reduces electric-shock risk by providing a preferred low-resistance path for leakage/fault current.
It helps protective devices operate quickly during earth faults and reduces fire risk.
Pipe earthing: a G.I. pipe electrode is buried vertically in moist soil; the surrounding soil is commonly treated with charcoal and salt and kept moist.
Plate earthing: a G.I. plate electrode is buried in the ground, surrounded by alternate layers of charcoal and salt and kept moist.
parts.result: The current R25 syllabus specifically requires pipe earthing and plate earthing.

questions.question: With neat Diagrams and Waveforms Explain the Operation of Full wave Rectifier.

paragraphs: A full-wave rectifier makes the load current flow in the same direction during both half cycles of the AC input. A centre-tapped two-diode circuit is one standard realisation; a bridge rectifier is another.
bullets: Positive half-cycle: the diode connected to the positive end of the secondary conducts; the other diode is reverse biased.
Negative half-cycle: the other end becomes positive relative to the centre tap, so the second diode conducts. Load current still has the same direction.
Output ripple frequency is \(2f\).

questions.question: State Thevenin’s theorem.

paragraphs: Any linear bilateral two-terminal network containing sources and resistances can be replaced, as seen from the terminals, by an equivalent voltage source \(V_{Th}\) in series with an equivalent resistance \(R_{Th}\).
bullets: \(V_{Th}\) is the open-circuit terminal voltage.
\(R_{Th}\) is the resistance seen from the terminals after independent voltage sources are short-circuited and independent current sources are open-circuited.

questions.question: Define the following terms: (i) RMS value (ii) Average value

parts.label: i
paragraphs: RMS value is the square root of the mean of the squares of the instantaneous values over one complete cycle. It is the DC-equivalent value that produces the same heating effect in a resistor.

parts.label: ii
paragraphs: Average value is the arithmetic mean of instantaneous values. For a symmetrical sinusoid the full-cycle average is zero, so the conventional AC average value is taken over one half-cycle.
equations: \[X_{avg}=\frac{2X_m}{\pi}\quad\text{for a sine wave over a half-cycle}\]

parts.label: b
paragraphs: For the induction motor, the torque-slip relation may be written in the form
bullets: Low-slip region: \(sX_2\ll R_2\), so \(T\propto s\). Torque rises nearly linearly with slip.

questions.question: State Superposition theorem and mention one application of it.

paragraphs: Superposition theorem states that in a linear network containing several independent sources, the current through or voltage across any element equals the algebraic sum of the responses produced by each independent source acting alone.
bullets: While considering one source, replace other independent voltage sources by short circuits and independent current sources by open circuits.
Application: finding a branch current or voltage in a multi-source linear DC network.

questions.r25_mapping: Unit III · DC motor / back emf
questions.question: What is the significance of back EMF in a DC motor?

paragraphs: Back emf \(E_b\) is the emf generated in the rotating armature that opposes the applied supply according to Lenz’s law.
bullets: It limits armature current during normal running: \(I_a=(V-E_b)/R_a\).
It gives the motor a self-regulating action: increased load slows the motor, reducing \(E_b\), which increases armature current and torque.
At starting, \(E_b=0\), so starting current is very high unless limited.

questions.question: Define slip and slip speed of a three-phase induction motor.

paragraphs: Slip speed is the difference between synchronous speed and rotor speed. Slip is this difference expressed as a fraction of synchronous speed.

questions.question: List any two advantages of a lead-acid battery.

bullets: It is rechargeable and can be used through many charge-discharge cycles.
It can deliver large currents and stores substantial energy, making it useful for automobile starting and backup/inverter duty.
It is a mature, widely available and comparatively economical battery technology.

question_parts.content: Explain the role of electrical energy in modern life and various engineering branches.

parts.label: a
paragraphs: Electrical energy is a convenient, controllable, clean-at-point-of-use and easily transmissible form of energy. It can be converted efficiently into light, heat, mechanical motion and electronic processing.
bullets: Domestic and commercial use: lighting, heating, cooling, refrigeration, appliances, computers and office equipment.
Industry: motors and machine drives, process equipment, lighting, ventilation, automation and control.
Transportation and communication: electric trains/EVs, communication systems and data infrastructure.
Medicine and services: X-ray, ECG and other electrically operated medical equipment.

Engineering relevance: electrical machines provide electromechanical conversion; electronics, communication, instrumentation and computing all depend on electrical energy. For CSE/IT, computers, servers, networking and embedded systems ultimately depend on a reliable electrical-energy supply.
Power systems convert primary/mechanical energy into electricity, transmit it to load centres, distribute it and finally utilise it.

parts.label: b
paragraphs: Kirchhoff’s laws are used with Ohm’s law to analyse electrical networks.
bullets: Kirchhoff’s Current Law (KCL): the algebraic sum of currents at a node is zero; equivalently, total current entering a node equals total current leaving it.
Kirchhoff’s Voltage Law (KVL): the algebraic sum of all voltage rises and drops around any closed loop is zero.
parts.note: A simple KCL example is \(I_1+I_2=I_3+I_4\). A simple KVL example is \(V_s=IR_1+IR_2\) for two series resistors.

questions.question: State and explain Thevenin’s theorem and apply it to solve for the circuit given below between terminals a and b.

figures.description: Circuit diagram supplied with Question 2: the network to be reduced to its Thevenin equivalent between terminals a and b.
figures.alt: 2025–26 Unit I Q2 circuit for Thevenin theorem: 25 V source through 5 ohm to a common node, 20 ohm to the bottom node, a 3 A upward current source to the same node, and a 4 ohm resistor from the node to terminal a; terminal b is the bottom node.

paragraphs: Thevenin’s theorem replaces the linear network seen from terminals a-b by a source \(V_{Th}\) in series with \(R_{Th}\).
steps: Open-circuit the terminals a-b. No current flows through the 4 Ω resistor, so \(V_a\) equals the main top-node voltage \(V\).
KCL at that node: \((V-25)/5+V/20-3=0\). Solving gives \(V=32\,V\). Hence \(V_{Th}=32\,V\).
To find \(R_{Th}\), deactivate the independent sources: short the 25 V source and open the 3 A current source.
Seen from a-b, the 4 Ω resistor is in series with \(5\parallel20=4\,\Omega\). Thus \(R_{Th}=4+4=8\,\Omega\).
answer.result: Thevenin equivalent at a-b: \(V_{Th}=32\,V\) in series with \(R_{Th}=8\,\Omega\).

groups.title: Unit II · Steady-state AC circuits
groups.note: In the paper, answer either Q3 or Q4.

questions.question: Analyze a series RLC circuit under sinusoidal excitation and derive expressions for current and impedance.

paragraphs: For a series RLC circuit supplied by sinusoidal RMS voltage \(V\), the same current \(I\) flows through R, L and C. Take current as the reference phasor.
bullets: If \(X_L>X_C\), the circuit is inductive and current lags voltage.
If \(X_C>X_L\), the circuit is capacitive and current leads voltage.
If \(X_L=X_C\), the circuit is at series resonance: \(Z=R\), current is maximum and power factor is unity.
answer.result: Series RLC impedance is \(Z=R+j(X_L-X_C)\); current is \(I=V/Z\).

questions.question: Explain three-phase balanced circuits and derive voltage and current relations for star and delta connections.

paragraphs: A balanced three-phase system has three sinusoidal phase quantities of equal magnitude and frequency displaced by 120°. A balanced load has identical impedances in all three phases.
answer.result: Balanced star: \(V_L=\sqrt3V_{ph}, I_L=I_{ph}\). Balanced delta: \(V_L=V_{ph}, I_L=\sqrt3I_{ph}\).

parts.label: Star (Y)
paragraphs: Each phase is connected from a line to the neutral point. Take \(V_{RN}=V_{ph}\angle0^\circ\) and \(V_{YN}=V_{ph}\angle-120^\circ\).
bullets: Each line conductor is in series with its phase, so line current equals phase current.
The line voltage leads the corresponding phase voltage by 30°.

parts.label: Delta (Δ)
paragraphs: Each phase is connected directly between two lines, hence \(V_L=V_{ph}\). At a line terminal the line current is the phasor difference of the two phase currents meeting there.
bullets: For the usual phase sequence, line current is displaced by 30° from the corresponding phase current.

groups.title: Unit III · Transformers and DC machines
groups.note: In the paper, answer either Q5 or Q6.

question_parts.label: a
question_parts.content: Explain the working principle of a transformer.

question_parts.label: b
question_parts.content: Derive the EMF equation of a DC generator from fundamentals.

parts.label: a
paragraphs: A transformer is a static device that transfers AC electrical energy from one circuit to another at the same frequency by electromagnetic induction.

When AC is applied to the primary winding, a small magnetising current produces alternating core flux. This flux links both windings and induces emfs in the primary and secondary according to Faraday’s law. If a load is connected to the secondary, secondary current flows and the primary draws the additional current needed to balance the secondary ampere-turns.
bullets: If \(N_2>N_1\), it is step-up; if \(N_2<N_1\), it is step-down.
A transformer does not operate on steady DC because steady DC does not create alternating flux.
parts.diagram: AC supply V1 → [Primary N1] ║ laminated iron core ║ [Secondary N2] → Load

parts.label: b
paragraphs: Let \(P\) be the number of poles, \(\Phi\) flux per pole, \(Z\) total armature conductors, \(N\) speed in rpm and \(A\) parallel paths.
bullets: For lap winding, \(A=P\).
For wave winding, \(A=2\).
steps: Flux cut by one conductor in one revolution = \(P\Phi\) Wb.
Average emf induced in one conductor = \(P\Phi /(60/N)=P\Phi N/60\) V.
Conductors in series per parallel path = \(Z/A\).

questions.r25_mapping: Unit III · Practical transformer / efficiency / regulation
questions.question: Explain the equivalent circuit of a practical transformer and derive expressions for efficiency and regulation.

paragraphs: A practical transformer includes winding resistance, leakage reactance, finite magnetising current and iron loss. Its equivalent circuit therefore contains primary series elements \(R_1,X_1\), secondary series elements \(R_2,X_2\), and a shunt branch representing core loss resistance \(R_0\) and magnetising reactance \(X_m\).
bullets: To refer secondary quantities to the primary: \(R_2' = R_2/k^2\), \(X_2' = X_2/k^2\), where \(k=N_2/N_1\).
Equivalent series resistance and reactance can then be combined on one side for regulation and efficiency calculations.
answer.diagram:
V1 → R1 → jX1 → [ideal transformer] → R2 → jX2 → Load
             │
             ├── R0 (core-loss branch)
             └── jXm (magnetising branch)
answer.note: The regulation expressions above follow the prescribed textbook convention used in the current Unit III text.

groups.title: Unit IV · Alternating-current machines
groups.note: In the paper, answer either Q7 or Q8.

question_parts.label: a
question_parts.content: Explain the principle of operation of a three-phase induction motor.

question_parts.label: b
question_parts.content: Explain torque–slip characteristics of an induction motor.

parts.label: a
paragraphs: A balanced three-phase supply to the stator windings produces a rotating magnetic field (RMF). The RMF rotates at synchronous speed.

Because the rotor initially has relative motion with respect to the RMF, an emf is induced in the short-circuited rotor conductors. Rotor current flows, and interaction of rotor current with the stator field produces torque in the direction of the RMF.
The rotor cannot reach synchronous speed in motoring operation: at synchronous speed the relative speed would be zero, rotor emf and rotor current would vanish, and therefore torque would be zero.
parts.result: The induction motor therefore runs slightly below synchronous speed with non-zero slip.

parts.label: b
paragraphs: For the induction motor, the torque-slip relation may be written in the form
bullets: Low-slip region: \(sX_2\ll R_2\), so \(T\propto s\). Torque rises nearly linearly with slip.
Maximum torque occurs at \(s=R_2/X_2\).
High-slip region: \(sX_2\gg R_2\), so \(T\propto 1/s\). Torque falls as slip increases.
At start, \(s=1\), giving the starting torque. At synchronous speed, \(s=0\) and torque is zero.
parts.result: The normal stable motoring region lies on the low-slip side of the maximum-torque point.

questions.question: Explain voltage regulation of a synchronous generator using synchronous impedance method.

paragraphs: The synchronous-impedance (EMF) method obtains an equivalent synchronous impedance from open-circuit and short-circuit tests at rated speed, then uses it to calculate the generated emf required for a specified load.
bullets: For lagging power factor the synchronous-reactance drop generally increases the required generated emf.
For leading power factor the phasor relation can reduce the required generated emf and regulation can become small or negative.
steps: Open-circuit test (OCC): run the alternator at rated speed with armature open and record terminal voltage versus field current.
Short-circuit test (SCC): run at rated speed with the armature terminals symmetrically shorted and record armature current versus field current.
For the same field current, use per-phase values to calculate \(Z_s=V_{OC}/I_{SC}\).
For the specified load current and power factor, use the generator phasor equation \(\mathbf E_0=\mathbf V+\mathbf I(R_a+jX_s)\) to obtain \(|E_0|\).
answer.result: OCC + SCC → \(Z_s\) → \(X_s\) → generated emf \(E_0\) → percentage voltage regulation.

groups.title: Unit V · Electrical installations and batteries
groups.note: In the paper, answer either Q9 or Q10.

question_parts.label: a
question_parts.content: Explain the basic layout of a domestic electrical installation.

question_parts.label: b
question_parts.content: Explain the need for earthing and types of earthing.

parts.label: a
paragraphs: In a single-phase domestic installation the load is supplied between phase and neutral at about 230 V. The incoming service passes through metering, main protection and a distribution board before reaching individual sub-circuits.
bullets: The service fuse protects the incoming service conductor.
The energy meter records electrical-energy consumption.
The main MCB controls and protects the whole installation.
The distribution board divides the supply into sub-circuits, each with its own protective MCB.
Metallic enclosures and exposed conductive parts are connected to earth.
parts.diagram:
Supply → service fuse → energy meter → main MCB → distribution board → sub-circuit MCBs → lights / fans / sockets / loads
Earth electrode ───────────────────────────────→ metal enclosures / earth conductors

parts.label: b
paragraphs: Earthing connects exposed metallic parts of electrical equipment to the earth through a low-resistance conductor and electrode.
bullets: It reduces electric-shock risk by providing a preferred low-resistance path for leakage/fault current.
It helps protective devices operate quickly during earth faults and reduces fire risk.
Pipe earthing: a G.I. pipe electrode is buried vertically in moist soil; the surrounding soil is commonly treated with charcoal and salt and kept moist.
Plate earthing: a G.I. plate electrode is buried in the ground, surrounded by alternate layers of charcoal and salt and kept moist.
parts.result: The current R25 syllabus specifically requires pipe earthing and plate earthing.

questions.question: Explain the construction, working and characteristics of a lead-acid battery and explain UPS operation with block diagram.

answer.result: Lead-acid battery provides rechargeable DC storage; the UPS uses stored battery energy through the inverter to keep the AC load energised during mains failure.

parts.label: Lead-acid battery
paragraphs: A lead-acid battery is a rechargeable secondary battery. The positive plate is lead dioxide \(PbO_2\), the negative plate is sponge lead \(Pb\), and the electrolyte is dilute sulphuric acid \(H_2SO_4\). Separators prevent direct contact between opposite plates. A cell gives about 2.1 V; six cells form a nominal 12 V battery.
bullets: Fully charged open-circuit voltage is stated as about 2.2 V per cell.
During discharge terminal voltage falls; the text advises not allowing it below about 1.8 V per cell.
Capacity is rated in ampere-hours (Ah) and falls as discharge rate rises.
Ah efficiency is typically about 90–95%; watt-hour efficiency is lower than Ah efficiency.

parts.label: UPS
paragraphs: A UPS maintains continuity of supply to critical AC loads when the normal AC source fails.
bullets: Normal supply present: the rectifier converts AC to DC, feeds the inverter and charges the battery.
AC supply failure: the battery supplies DC to the inverter; the inverter converts it to AC and the filter supplies the critical load.
The UPS also helps regulate/condition the output voltage supplied to the critical load.
parts.diagram:
AC input → Rectifier → DC link → Inverter → Filter → Critical load
                         ↕
                      Battery bank
